methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $15M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 12 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring
methods.skip_reason: target revenue not on file (private companies rarely disclose)
methods.rationale: Public Semiconductors P/S median is 21.0x across 3 tickers. Cannot apply without target's revenue.

data.narrative:
Fab2, a Seed-stage semiconductor company founded by Jim Keller and Sam Zeloof, has raised $15M+ to date. The Chips & Semiconductors sector includes 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers such as Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, and SambaNova Systems, though none offer sufficiently tight valuation anchors at the same stage.

Stage-Progression modeling is the primary applicable method, using the $15M total raised as a proxy for Seed-stage value and applying a standard 2.5x step-up multiplier to approximate next-stage valuation. This yields $38M. Peer-Median triangulation is not supportable: while 12 same-sector peers exist in the comparable universe, insufficient datapoints meet narrow filters (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier) to construct a reliable median. Public-Comp anchoring via P/S multiples—the sector median is 21.0x across the three public tickers—cannot be applied without Fab2's revenue, which is not disclosed.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $32M to $43M, centered on $38M, derived from a single method. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 2.5x multiplier absent tight peer comparables, the lack of revenue data to cross-check against public multiples, and limited visibility into the Seed-stage financing patterns specific to hardware-intensive semiconductor ventures. Broader triangulation would require additional financial disclosure from the target or identification of closer-stage peers.
